b2-eszmetortenet-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Széchenyi's Offer
b2-eszmetortenet-01.scenario: At the Hungarian Academy of Sciences in Budapest, a guide asks you what Count István Széchenyi did in 1825 and what he thought held the country back.
b2-eszmetortenet-01.prompt: Tell the guide what Széchenyi offered in 1825 and what he saw as the cause of backwardness.
cues: Say what he offered for the learned society
Say what he saw as the cause of backwardness
b2-eszmetortenet-01.target: Széchenyi 1825-ben birtokainak egyéves jövedelmét ajánlotta fel a tudós társaság megalapítására. Szerinte az elmaradottság oka nem más, mint a tőkehiány és a feudális jogrendszer.
b2-eszmetortenet-01.english: In 1825 Széchenyi offered one year's income from his estates to found the learned society. In his view the cause of backwardness was none other than the shortage of capital and the feudal legal system.
b2-eszmetortenet-01.canDo: I can say what Count István Széchenyi offered, wrote and built: the Academy, the Hitel and the Chain Bridge.

b2-eszmetortenet-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Eötvös and the 1868 Laws
b2-eszmetortenet-02.scenario: In a seminar on Hungarian liberalism, a lecturer asks you about Baron József Eötvös and the school law of 1868.
b2-eszmetortenet-02.prompt: Tell the lecturer what the 1868 school law introduced and what mattered most to Eötvös.
cues: Say what the school law introduced
Say what the decisive point was for Eötvös
b2-eszmetortenet-02.target: Az 1868-as népiskolai törvény jelentősége abban rejlett, hogy bevezette a tankötelezettséget. Eötvös szerint nem az a döntő szempont, hogy mekkora a hatalom, hanem az, hogy milyen törvényes korlátai vannak.
b2-eszmetortenet-02.english: The significance of the 1868 school law lay in that it introduced compulsory schooling. According to Eötvös the decisive point is not how large the power is, but what legal limits it has.
b2-eszmetortenet-02.canDo: I can explain Baron József Eötvös's view of the limits of state power and the 1868 school and nationality laws.

b2-eszmetortenet-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Polányi's Critique
b2-eszmetortenet-03.scenario: At a book fair in Budapest, a student asks you what Karl Polanyi criticised in his book The Great Transformation.
b2-eszmetortenet-03.prompt: Tell the student what Karl Polanyi criticised and how he explained the crisis of the market economy.
cues: Say what caused the crisis, in his view
b2-eszmetortenet-03.target: Polányi Károly bírálta az önszabályozó piacot. Szerinte a válság abból adódott, hogy a föld, a munka és a pénz áruvá vált.
b2-eszmetortenet-03.english: Karl Polanyi criticised the self-regulating market. In his view the crisis arose from the fact that land, labour and money became commodities.
b2-eszmetortenet-03.canDo: I can outline Karl Polanyi's critique of the self-regulating market in 'The Great Transformation' (A nagy átalakulás).

b2-eszmetortenet-04.title: Communicative Challenge: 4 November 1956
b2-eszmetortenet-04.scenario: In a café near the Parliament in Budapest, a history student asks you where Bibó István was on 4 November 1956 and what he wrote about political hysteria.
b2-eszmetortenet-04.prompt: Tell the student where Bibó stayed on 4 November 1956 and what he saw as the nature of political hysteria.
cues: Say what the nature of political hysteria is, in his view
b2-eszmetortenet-04.target: Bibó István 1956. november 4-én a Parlamentben maradt. Szerinte a politikai hisztéria természete éppen abban áll, hogy a közösség bűnbakokat keres.
b2-eszmetortenet-04.english: Bibó István stayed in the Parliament on 4 November 1956. In his view the nature of political hysteria consists precisely in that the community looks for scapegoats.
b2-eszmetortenet-04.canDo: I can summarize István Bibó's diagnosis of political hysteria in small Eastern European states.

b2-eszmetortenet-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Four Thinkers Today
b2-eszmetortenet-05.scenario: At a conference at the Academy of Sciences, a participant asks you what the four thinkers still mean to readers today.
b2-eszmetortenet-05.prompt: Tell the participant what many interpreters see as the common message of the four thinkers.
cues: Say what freedom and responsibility are
b2-eszmetortenet-05.target: Sok értelmező szerint a magyar gondolkodók közös üzenete nem más, mint az, hogy a szabadság és a felelősség elválaszthatatlanok egymástól.
b2-eszmetortenet-05.english: According to many interpreters, the common message of Hungarian thinkers is none other than that freedom and responsibility are inseparable from one another.
b2-eszmetortenet-05.canDo: I can say what many interpreters see as the common message of the four thinkers.

b2-eszmetortenet-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Three Thinkers in Three Sentences
b2-eszmetortenet-consolidation.scenario: At the end of a walking tour of the Academy and the Chain Bridge, the guide asks you to say one thing about Széchenyi, one about Polányi Mihály and one about Bibó.
b2-eszmetortenet-consolidation.prompt: Say one thing about each of the three thinkers.
cues: Say what Polányi Mihály said about skilled knowledge
Say what Bibó saw as the essence of democratic conduct
b2-eszmetortenet-consolidation.target: Széchenyi 1825-ben birtokainak egyéves jövedelmét ajánlotta fel a tudós társaság megalapítására. Polányi Mihály szerint a mesterségbeli tudás nem fejezhető ki teljesen szabályokkal. Bibó szerint a demokratikus magatartás lényege a félelemnélküliség.
b2-eszmetortenet-consolidation.english: In 1825 Széchenyi offered one year's income from his estates to found the learned society. According to Michael Polanyi, skilled knowledge cannot be fully expressed in rules. According to Bibó, the essence of democratic conduct is fearlessness.
b2-eszmetortenet-consolidation.canDo: I can say what Széchenyi, Michael Polanyi and Bibó are each known for.
